B. ENTIRE LOGICAL DOCUMENT DELETION - An authorized user may request deletion of the entire logical document, including all associated versions. - This operation must require explicit confirmation of the complete deletion scope. - All versions and associated derived content must be included. - This operation must not be treated as multiple unrelated single-version deletion requests.  2. REQUEST, APPROVAL AND EXECUTION AUTHORITY  - Authorized document owners or tenant users with appropriate permissions may submit deletion requests within their own tenant. - The Tenant Admin is responsible for reviewing and authorizing deletion requests. - The requester and approver must be different individuals. - If the requesting user is the Tenant Admin, an independently authorized second Tenant Admin must approve the request. AUDIT RETENTION  - All deletion requests, approvals, retries, failures, deadline breaches, escalations, and verification outcomes must be recorded. - Content-free deletion audit evidence must be retained for the established 365-day period. - Audit records must be protected from unauthorized modification or deletion. - The audit trail must allow reconstruction of the deletion lifecycle without preserving the deleted business content.  9. These deferrals do not waive the 24-hour purge requirement, permit retrieval of excluded content, or authorize reporting unverified deletion as successful.  This policy preserves the established 24-hour primary-storage purge, 30-day encrypted-backup expiry, and 365-day content-free audit-retention requirements., backup_audit=30-DAY ENCRYPTED BACKUP AND 365-DAY CONTENT-FREE AUDIT RETENTION POLICY  1. ENCRYPTED BACKUP RETENTION — 30 DAYS  Confirm and adopt the proposed maximum 30-day encrypted-backup age-out requirement.  - The 30-day retention clock starts from the creation timestamp of each individual backup. - Backup creation timestamps must be recorded in UTC. - Each backup must automatically expire and become unavailable after a maximum of 30 days. - Backups must remain encrypted and protected against unauthorized access throughout their retention period. - Deleting an individual document must not require immediate deletion of an entire backup containing unrelated tenant data. - Backup expiry must be independently tracked and auditable. - No ordinary administrative or business convenience exception may extend the 30-day backup retention period.  2. CONTENT-FREE AUDIT RETENTION — 365 DAYS  Confirm and adopt the proposed 365-day content-free deletion and audit metadata retention requirement.  - The retention clock starts when each audit record is created. - Each record must be retained for 365 days from its creation timestamp. - The audit trail must include deletion requests, approvals, execution events, retries, failures, deadline breaches, verification results, and backup expiry evidence. - Audit records must remain content-free and must not contain original documents, extracted text, chunks, embeddings, passwords, access tokens, or other sensitive content. - After the applicable 365-day period, records must be removed through an authorized, controlled audit-retention process. - Audit retention and document-content retention must remain separate policies.  3. BACKUP RESTORATION AND DELETION REAPPLICATION  Backup restoration must never reintroduce previously deleted content into active systems.  Before restored data becomes accessible to users or AI retrieval:  - All applicable deletion records and suppression controls must be reapplied. - Documents and versions previously approved for deletion must remain excluded. - Original files, extracted text, chunks, embeddings, search-index entries, and caches associated with deleted content must be removed or suppressed. - Previously expired, rejected, superseded, and overdue content must retain its applicable lifecycle and retrieval restrictions. - Restoration must not reset deletion deadlines or make previously deleted content eligible again. - The restoration process must verify deletion compliance before enabling normal application access.  4. EXCEPTION AUTHORITY  - No ordinary Platform Admin, Tenant Admin, Support Manager, or Support Agent may independently extend these retention periods. - No discretionary administrative exception is permitted in the first release. - A formally documented mandatory legal or regulatory retention obligation may justify a narrowly scoped exception only with explicit authorization from the designated Legal Authority and independent Security review. - Any such exception must identify the legal basis, affected data, tenant, authorized scope, approving authority, and required retention period. - Legally retained content must remain excluded from AI retrieval unless separately and legitimately authorized. - Legal retention must not grant Platform Admin tenant-content access. - All exceptions and their subsequent release or expiry must be auditable.  5. RELATIONSHIP WITH Q4 RETENTION DEFERRALS  The retention details deferred during Q4 concerned lifecycle-specific retention periods for failed, rejected, superseded, expired, and overdue knowledge versions.  Those deferrals do not waive, suspend, or modify the separately established Q5 obligations:  - 24-hour primary-storage purge following explicit deletion approval. - Maximum 30-day encrypted-backup age-out from each backup's creation timestamp. - 365-day content-free audit retention from each audit record's creation timestamp.  The deferred lifecycle-specific retention schedule remains unresolved and requires separate governed clarification.  6. SECURITY AND GOVERNANCE CONSISTENCY  These requirements must preserve:  - Strict tenant isolation. - No exceptional Platform Admin tenant-content access in the first release. - Immediate retrieval exclusion after authorized deletion. - Prevention of deleted-content restoration. - Content-free and tamper-resistant audit evidence. - Controlled and independently authorized retention exceptions.  These decisions confirm the first-release backup and audit retention requirements. They do not authorize PRD approval, implementation, or any bypass of established deletion and access restrictions., rationale_deferrals=RATIONALE AND EXPLICIT REMAINING DEFERRALS — Q5 DELETION AND RETENTION  1. RATIONALE FOR THE FIRST-RELEASE POLICY  The selected deletion and retention policy provides a controlled, auditable, and tenant-isolated approach to managing knowledge content throughout its lifecycle.  It deliberately separates three different responsibilities:  - Immediate exclusion of deleted or ineligible content from AI retrieval and citation. - Physical removal of authorized deletion targets from active primary storage. - Limited retention of encrypted backups and content-free audit evidence.  This separation ensures that retaining historical or backup data does not imply continued permission to use that content for AI answers.  2. DELETION SCOPE AND AUTHORITY  Supporting both single-version deletion and entire logical document deletion provides operational flexibility while preventing accidental removal of unrelated versions.  Independent Tenant Admin authorization and controlled background execution establish accountability and reduce unauthorized or accidental deletion.  Platform Admins must not gain tenant-content access or deletion authority through administrative privileges.  3. RETRIEVAL SAFETY AND PHYSICAL PURGE  Immediate retrieval exclusion following explicit deletion approval ensures that deleted content cannot continue influencing AI-generated answers while physical deletion is in progress.  The mandatory 24-hour primary-storage purge requirement provides a measurable deletion deadline covering originals, extracted text, chunks, embeddings, indexes, caches, and other active derived copies.  Failure handling, retries, verification, and escalation ensure that deletion is not reported as successful before completion is established.  4. BACKUP AND AUDIT RETENTION RATIONALE  The maximum 30-day encrypted-backup age-out provides a bounded backup retention period without requiring deletion of unrelated content from shared backups.  The 365-day content-free audit retention provides evidence of deletion authorization, execution, failures, deadline breaches, verification, and accountability without preserving deleted business content.  Backup retention and audit retention are independent obligations with separate starting timestamps.  5. LIFECYCLE-STATE RETENTION RATIONALE  Failed, rejected, superseded, expired, and overdue content must remain excluded from AI retrieval.  Authorized human-only inspection may be permitted where operationally justified and explicitly authorized.  Physical retention and AI retrieval eligibility must remain separate decisions.  The mandatory 180-day independent re-review policy remains unchanged.  6. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED RETENTION DETAILS  The following lifecycle-specific retention durations remain unresolved:  - Failed document retention. - Rejected document retention. - Superseded version retention. - Expired document retention. - Overdue and pending-re-review content retention.  These periods require separate business, legal, regulatory, and operational assessment before being finalized.  Their deferral does not imply indefinite retention or override an authorized deletion request.  7. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED TECHNICAL DETAILS  The following implementation details are deferred to technical design:  - Exact backup infrastructure and automated expiry implementation. - Audit storage architecture and long-term evidence protection. - Component-specific deletion verification mechanisms. - Retry intervals, retry limits, and backoff configuration. - Monitoring, notification, and operational escalation SLAs. - Backup restoration validation implementation. - Detailed retention scheduling and lifecycle cleanup mechanisms.  These deferrals do not waive any established first-release deletion or retention obligation.  8. LEGAL HOLD AND RETENTION EXCEPTIONS  No legal hold, regulatory retention exception, or discretionary retention extension is implied merely because a requirement has been deferred.  The first release must not introduce an undocumented legal-hold or retention-exception bypass.  If a mandatory legal or regulatory retention obligation arises, it must be handled through a separately authorized and documented process that explicitly identifies:  - Applicable legal or regulatory basis. - Exact tenant and affected data scope. - Authorized approving Legal Authority. - Independent Security review. - Permitted retention duration and review conditions. - Access restrictions and AI retrieval exclusion. - Release or expiry conditions and audit evidence.  Any exception must remain limited to its explicitly approved scope and must not grant Platform Admin tenant-content access.  9. PRESERVATION OF PREVIOUS GOVERNANCE DECISIONS  All previously established Q2, Q3, and Q4 decisions remain unchanged, including:  - Independent non-submitter knowledge approval. - Mandatory 180-day re-review. - Tenant-scoped authorization and least privilege. - Prohibition of self-approval and privilege escalation. - Strict tenant isolation. - Prohibition of exceptional Platform Admin tenant-content access in the first release.  The Q4 technical and lifecycle retention deferrals do not waive the Q5 obligations.  The following Q5 requirements remain decided and mandatory:  - Immediate AI retrieval exclusion following authorized deletion. - Maximum 24-hour primary-storage purge. - Maximum 30-day encrypted-backup age-out. - 365-day content-free audit retention. - Verified deletion and controlled failure escalation.  10. FINAL FIRST-RELEASE POSITION  The first release prioritizes reliable deletion, immediate AI retrieval safety, bounded backup retention, content-free auditability, and strict tenant isolation.  Unresolved lifecycle-specific retention periods and technical implementation details remain explicitly deferred rather than assumed or silently waived.  These decisions clarify the Q5 requirements only. They do not constitute PRD approval, implementation authorization, or permission to bypass any established security or deletion control.

actual_fields.purge_clock: IMMEDIATE RETRIEVAL EXCLUSION AND 24-HOUR PHYSICAL PURGE DEADLINE POLICY  1. actual_fields.lifecycle_retention: KNOWLEDGE RETENTION BY LIFECYCLE STATE POLICY  1. REJECTED DOCUMENTS  - Rejected documents and versions must remain permanently excluded from AI retrieval unless a new, separately submitted and independently approved version becomes eligible. - Authorized Knowledge Reviewers and relevant document owners may inspect rejected content and rejection reasons for legitimate review and correction purposes. - Rejection must not automatically trigger physical deletion. - The rejected version must remain distinguishable from current approved knowledge. - The retention and automatic deletion period for rejected content is explicitly deferred pending a governed retention schedule.  4. SUPERSEDED DOCUMENTS AND VERSIONS  - Superseded versions must not be used for AI retrieval, search answers, or citations. - They may be retained for authorized human-only historical inspection, version comparison, audit, and investigation. - Only the currently approved and otherwise valid version may be eligible for AI retrieval. - Replacing an older version must not automatically delete the older version. - The retention duration and eventual deletion schedule for superseded versions are explicitly deferred.  5. EXPIRED DOCUMENTS AND VERSIONS  - Expired documents must immediately become ineligible for AI retrieval and citation. - Their content may be retained for authorized human-only historical or administrative inspection where justified. - Expiry must not be interpreted as automatic physical deletion. - Reapproval or an explicitly authorized validity extension must be completed before the document becomes AI eligible again. - The retention duration and automatic deletion policy for expired content are explicitly deferred.  6. actual_fields.purge_failure: DELETION FAILURE HANDLING, RETRIES, ESCALATION AND PROOF OF DELETION POLICY  1. AUTOMATIC RETRIES AND FAILURE HANDLING  - Transient storage, indexing, cache, and processing failures must trigger controlled automatic retries. - Retry operations must be idempotent and must not recreate content that has already been successfully deleted. - The worker must track successful, failed, and pending operations separately for each affected component. - Persistent failures must be escalated to designated Operations / Security personnel for investigation and resolution. - Exact retry intervals, retry limits, backoff strategy, and operational escalation SLAs are explicitly deferred to technical design. - Deferred retry details must not weaken the mandatory 24-hour primary-storage purge deadline.  3. 24-HOUR DEADLINE BREACH  - The 24-hour purge deadline remains mandatory from the explicit authorized approval timestamp. - If all required primary-storage deletion operations are not verified within 24 hours, the deletion must be marked Overdue. - The system must generate an auditable deadline-breach event and notify the responsible Operations / Security personnel and affected Tenant Admin. - The requesting user must receive an accurate status notification. - The affected content must remain permanently excluded from AI retrieval and citation. - An overdue deletion must never be silently reported as successful. - Operational investigation and retry must continue until completion or an explicitly documented resolution.  4. Deadline Breach: - Notify the Tenant Admin and designated Operations / Security personnel. - Clearly identify that the 24-hour purge deadline has been missed. - Provide the request reference, failure status, and escalation information. Completion evidence must include: - Deletion request ID and affected tenant/document/version references. - Component category and deletion operation outcome. - Execution timestamp and verification timestamp. - Deletion worker or system identity. - Retry count and failure information, where applicable. - Final verification result. - Overall deletion completion timestamp. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED TECHNICAL DETAILS  The following are deferred to subsequent technical design:  - Exact automatic retry intervals and maximum retry count. - Exponential backoff and retry scheduling configuration. - Detailed alert severity levels and escalation SLAs. - Specific monitoring and observability platform integration. - Component-specific verification implementation. - Operational dashboards and notification delivery mechanisms. IN-FLIGHT REQUEST AND PROCESSING HANDLING  - AI requests already in progress must not return or cite content covered by an approved deletion. - Pending retrieval operations involving the affected content must be cancelled or have their results discarded. - Any response generation dependent on affected content must be stopped or regenerated without that content before delivery. - Background extraction, chunking, embedding, indexing, and reprocessing jobs for the affected deletion scope must be cancelled or prevented from publishing new derived content. - Deletion-state checks must prevent delayed or retried processing jobs from recreating deleted content. - Cache invalidation must apply across all relevant application instances and retrieval services.  4. SCOPE OF THE 24-HOUR PHYSICAL-PURGE DEADLINE  The 24-hour deadline covers all affected active primary-storage originals and derived content, including:  - Original uploaded files. - Extracted text and content-bearing metadata. - Document chunks and excerpts. - Vector embeddings and associated vector database entries. - Search index entries and searchable representations. - Application and retrieval caches. - Temporary processing files and intermediate content. - Other active primary-storage copies derived from the affected document or versions.  For entire logical document deletion, the deadline covers every associated version and all their derived artifacts.  For single-version deletion, unrelated versions must remain unaffected.  5. BACKUP AGE-OUT IS A SEPARATE REQUIREMENT  - The 24-hour deadline applies to active primary storage and associated active derived copies. - Encrypted backup copies are governed by the separately established maximum 30-day backup age-out policy. - Deleted content must not become available again through backup restoration. - Backup restoration must reapply applicable deletion records before restored content becomes available to any user or AI retrieval process.  6. FAILURE HANDLING AND VERIFICATION  - The system must track deletion progress across all relevant storage and processing components. - Each purge operation must be traceable to the original approved deletion request. - Failures must be recorded, retried safely, and escalated for operational resolution. - The system must not report deletion as complete until all required primary-storage purge operations have been verified. - If any operation remains incomplete at the 24-hour deadline, the deletion must be reported as overdue or failed, remain excluded from retrieval, and trigger an auditable operational alert. - Repeated execution must be idempotent and must not recreate previously deleted content.  7. AUDITABILITY  Record: - Deletion request ID. - Requester and approving administrator. - Tenant and affected document/version identifiers. - Explicit approval timestamp in UTC. - Calculated 24-hour purge deadline. - Immediate retrieval-exclusion timestamp. - Cache invalidation and in-flight request handling outcomes. - Primary-storage purge results for each relevant component. - Backup expiry tracking status. - Failure, retry, escalation, and final verification timestamps.  Audit records must remain content-free under the established 365-day audit-retention policy.  These rules preserve the previously established 24-hour primary-storage purge, 30-day encrypted-backup expiry, and 365-day content-free audit-retention requirements.,

lifecycle_retention.exact_rendered_segment: KNOWLEDGE RETENTION BY LIFECYCLE STATE POLICY  1. GENERAL RETENTION PRINCIPLES  - Retention and AI retrieval eligibility must be treated as separate decisions. - Retaining a document or version for historical, administrative, or audit purposes must never automatically make it eligible for AI retrieval or citation. - All non-current, rejected, failed, expired, superseded, and overdue content must remain excluded from AI retrieval. - Human inspection is permitted only for explicitly authorized users within the applicable tenant and role boundaries. - Retention periods not yet established are explicitly deferred and must not be silently assumed to be indefinite. - Authorized deletion requests remain governed by the established Q5 deletion and purge policy.  2. FAILED DOCUMENTS  - Documents that fail upload validation, extraction, processing, indexing, or other required processing stages must remain ineligible for AI retrieval. - Authorized tenant administrators and relevant operational personnel may inspect failed-document metadata and processing diagnostics. - Original content may be accessed only by explicitly authorized personnel where necessary for troubleshooting. - Failed documents must not be automatically approved or made searchable following successful reprocessing. - Any successfully reprocessed document must complete the established independent review and approval lifecycle before becoming AI eligible. - The specific retention and automatic deletion period for failed documents is explicitly deferred pending a governed retention schedule.  3. REJECTED DOCUMENTS  - Rejected documents and versions must remain permanently excluded from AI retrieval unless a new, separately submitted and independently approved version becomes eligible. - Authorized Knowledge Reviewers and relevant document owners may inspect rejected content and rejection reasons for legitimate review and correction purposes. - Rejection must not automatically trigger physical deletion. - The rejected version must remain distinguishable from current approved knowledge. - The retention and automatic deletion period for rejected content is explicitly deferred pending a governed retention schedule.  4. SUPERSEDED DOCUMENTS AND VERSIONS  - Superseded versions must not be used for AI retrieval, search answers, or citations. - They may be retained for authorized human-only historical inspection, version comparison, audit, and investigation. - Only the currently approved and otherwise valid version may be eligible for AI retrieval. - Replacing an older version must not automatically delete the older version. - The retention duration and eventual deletion schedule for superseded versions are explicitly deferred.  5. EXPIRED DOCUMENTS AND VERSIONS  - Expired documents must immediately become ineligible for AI retrieval and citation. - Their content may be retained for authorized human-only historical or administrative inspection where justified. - Expiry must not be interpreted as automatic physical deletion. - Reapproval or an explicitly authorized validity extension must be completed before the document becomes AI eligible again. - The retention duration and automatic deletion policy for expired content are explicitly deferred.  6. OVERDUE AND PENDING RE-REVIEW DOCUMENTS  - The established 180-day re-review policy remains mandatory. - Once the applicable 180-day period expires without successful independent reapproval, the affected document version must immediately become ineligible for AI retrieval and citation. - The overdue version may remain available for authorized human-only review and investigation. - Continued physical retention must not imply continued validity or AI eligibility. - An older version remaining current until its replacement is approved does not override its own validity, authorization, or 180-day review restrictions. - Reinstatement requires explicit independent human approval and satisfaction of all current validity and authorization conditions. - Clarification alone, automated flags, or successful reprocessing must not reset the 180-day clock. - The separate retention and eventual deletion period for overdue content is explicitly deferred.  7. HUMAN-ONLY RETENTION AND ACCESS RESTRICTIONS  Human-only retained content must: - Remain tenant-scoped. - Be accessible only to explicitly authorized users with legitimate operational, review, or administrative responsibilities. - Remain excluded from AI retrieval, citation, and answer generation. - Not be exposed through ordinary user-facing Knowledge Search. - Not become accessible to Platform Admins through privileged administrative access. - Respect all established confidentiality, authorization, and audit requirements.  8. RETENTION PERIODS AND DELETION GOVERNANCE  The exact automatic retention and deletion periods for failed, rejected, superseded, expired, and overdue content are explicitly deferred.  They require separate review of business requirements, applicable legal obligations, customer retention expectations, and storage considerations.  This deferral does not: - Grant indefinite retention authority. - Allow excluded content to become AI eligible. - Override an authorized deletion request. - Suspend the previously accepted 24-hour primary-storage purge requirement. - Change the 30-day encrypted-backup age-out policy. - Change the 365-day content-free audit-retention policy.  9. PRESERVATION OF EXISTING GOVERNANCE  All previously established Q2, Q3, and Q5 rules remain applicable, including:  - Independent non-submitter approval. - Mandatory 180-day re-review. - Immediate retrieval exclusion for overdue content. - Human-controlled resolution and reinstatement. - Tenant-scoped access restrictions. - Authorized deletion and physical purge. - Separation of content retention from AI retrieval eligibility.  This decision defines lifecycle-state retention and eligibility requirements only. It does not authorize implementation or change previously approved governance boundaries.,

purge_failure.exact_rendered_segment: DELETION FAILURE HANDLING, RETRIES, ESCALATION AND PROOF OF DELETION POLICY  1. FAILURE OWNERSHIP AND RESPONSIBILITY  - The tenant-scoped Background Deletion Service is responsible for executing authorized deletion operations. - The deletion worker must manage retries for transient failures and track the completion status of every affected storage and derived-data component. - Designated Platform Operations / Security personnel are responsible for monitoring deletion failures and investigating operational issues. - Tenant Admins must be notified of deletion failures and deadline breaches affecting their tenant. - The deletion service must operate through narrowly scoped system identities and must not grant Platform Admins tenant-content access. - No individual may bypass the established deletion authorization or tenant-isolation controls to resolve a deletion failure.  2. AUTOMATIC RETRIES AND FAILURE HANDLING  - Transient storage, indexing, cache, and processing failures must trigger controlled automatic retries. - Retry operations must be idempotent and must not recreate content that has already been successfully deleted. - The worker must track successful, failed, and pending operations separately for each affected component. - Persistent failures must be escalated to designated Operations / Security personnel for investigation and resolution. - Exact retry intervals, retry limits, backoff strategy, and operational escalation SLAs are explicitly deferred to technical design. - Deferred retry details must not weaken the mandatory 24-hour primary-storage purge deadline.  3. 24-HOUR DEADLINE BREACH  - The 24-hour purge deadline remains mandatory from the explicit authorized approval timestamp. - If all required primary-storage deletion operations are not verified within 24 hours, the deletion must be marked Overdue. - The system must generate an auditable deadline-breach event and notify the responsible Operations / Security personnel and affected Tenant Admin. - The requesting user must receive an accurate status notification. - The affected content must remain permanently excluded from AI retrieval and citation. - An overdue deletion must never be silently reported as successful. - Operational investigation and retry must continue until completion or an explicitly documented resolution.  4. USER AND ADMINISTRATOR NOTIFICATIONS  The system must provide clear notifications for the following events:  A. Deletion Request Approved: - Confirm that deletion has been authorized. - Communicate that AI retrieval and citation access have been immediately disabled. - Provide the deletion request reference and applicable purge deadline.  B. Deletion In Progress: - Indicate that physical deletion is ongoing. - Do not claim that deletion is complete.  C. Partial Failure: - Inform the Tenant Admin that some deletion operations remain incomplete. - Identify affected component categories and operational status without exposing sensitive content. - Indicate that retrieval exclusion remains enforced.  D. Deadline Breach: - Notify the Tenant Admin and designated Operations / Security personnel. - Clearly identify that the 24-hour purge deadline has been missed. - Provide the request reference, failure status, and escalation information.  E. Verified Completion: - Notify the requester and Tenant Admin that the required primary-storage purge has been successfully verified. - Provide the deletion request reference and completion timestamp. - Clarify that encrypted backup age-out remains subject to the separate 30-day policy.  5. PARTIAL FAILURE AND DELETION STATUS  The system must maintain explicit deletion states, including:  - DeletionPending: Approved deletion awaiting execution. - RetrievalExcluded: AI retrieval and citation are blocked. - Purging: Physical deletion is in progress. - PartiallyPurged: Some required components are deleted while others remain. - PurgeFailed: A required deletion operation has failed. - Overdue: The mandatory 24-hour deadline has been exceeded. - Purged: All required primary-storage deletion operations have been independently verified.  A single successful component deletion must not mark the entire request as Purged.  Partial failure must remain visible and auditable until all required deletion operations are completed and verified.  6. PROOF OF DELETION AND COMPLETION VERIFICATION  The system must maintain verifiable evidence for each affected component category, including:  - Original file storage. - Extracted text and content-bearing metadata. - Document chunks and excerpts. - Vector embeddings and vector database entries. - Search index representations. - Application and retrieval caches. - Temporary processing files and intermediate content. - Other affected active primary-storage copies.  Completion evidence must include: - Deletion request ID and affected tenant/document/version references. - Component category and deletion operation outcome. - Execution timestamp and verification timestamp. - Deletion worker or system identity. - Retry count and failure information, where applicable. - Final verification result. - Overall deletion completion timestamp.  Verification must establish that the affected content is no longer available in the relevant active primary-storage systems or AI retrieval paths.  Audit evidence must remain content-free and must not contain deleted document contents, extracted text, chunks, embeddings, credentials, or secrets.  7. BACKUP AND RESTORATION DISTINCTION  - Primary-storage deletion verification and encrypted-backup expiry verification must be treated as separate obligations. - A deletion may be marked as primary-storage Purged only after all required active primary-storage components have been verified. - Backup copies remain governed by the maximum 30-day encrypted-backup age-out policy. - Backup restoration must reapply deletion records before restored content becomes accessible. - Primary-storage deletion success must not be interpreted as proof that backup expiry has already completed.  8. AUDIT RETENTION  - All deletion requests, approvals, retries, failures, deadline breaches, escalations, and verification outcomes must be recorded. - Content-free deletion audit evidence must be retained for the established 365-day period. - Audit records must be protected from unauthorized modification or deletion. - The audit trail must allow reconstruction of the deletion lifecycle without preserving the deleted business content.  9. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED TECHNICAL DETAILS  The following are deferred to subsequent technical design:  - Exact automatic retry intervals and maximum retry count. - Exponential backoff and retry scheduling configuration. - Detailed alert severity levels and escalation SLAs. - Specific monitoring and observability platform integration. - Component-specific verification implementation. - Operational dashboards and notification delivery mechanisms.  These deferrals do not waive the 24-hour purge requirement, permit retrieval of excluded content, or authorize reporting unverified deletion as successful.  This policy preserves the established 24-hour primary-storage purge, 30-day encrypted-backup expiry, and 365-day content-free audit-retention requirements.,

backup_audit.exact_rendered_segment: 30-DAY ENCRYPTED BACKUP AND 365-DAY CONTENT-FREE AUDIT RETENTION POLICY  1. ENCRYPTED BACKUP RETENTION — 30 DAYS  Confirm and adopt the proposed maximum 30-day encrypted-backup age-out requirement.  - The 30-day retention clock starts from the creation timestamp of each individual backup. - Backup creation timestamps must be recorded in UTC. - Each backup must automatically expire and become unavailable after a maximum of 30 days. - Backups must remain encrypted and protected against unauthorized access throughout their retention period. - Deleting an individual document must not require immediate deletion of an entire backup containing unrelated tenant data. - Backup expiry must be independently tracked and auditable. - No ordinary administrative or business convenience exception may extend the 30-day backup retention period.  2. CONTENT-FREE AUDIT RETENTION — 365 DAYS  Confirm and adopt the proposed 365-day content-free deletion and audit metadata retention requirement.  - The retention clock starts when each audit record is created. - Each record must be retained for 365 days from its creation timestamp. - The audit trail must include deletion requests, approvals, execution events, retries, failures, deadline breaches, verification results, and backup expiry evidence. - Audit records must remain content-free and must not contain original documents, extracted text, chunks, embeddings, passwords, access tokens, or other sensitive content. - After the applicable 365-day period, records must be removed through an authorized, controlled audit-retention process. - Audit retention and document-content retention must remain separate policies.  3. BACKUP RESTORATION AND DELETION REAPPLICATION  Backup restoration must never reintroduce previously deleted content into active systems.  Before restored data becomes accessible to users or AI retrieval:  - All applicable deletion records and suppression controls must be reapplied. - Documents and versions previously approved for deletion must remain excluded. - Original files, extracted text, chunks, embeddings, search-index entries, and caches associated with deleted content must be removed or suppressed. - Previously expired, rejected, superseded, and overdue content must retain its applicable lifecycle and retrieval restrictions. - Restoration must not reset deletion deadlines or make previously deleted content eligible again. - The restoration process must verify deletion compliance before enabling normal application access.  4. EXCEPTION AUTHORITY  - No ordinary Platform Admin, Tenant Admin, Support Manager, or Support Agent may independently extend these retention periods. - No discretionary administrative exception is permitted in the first release. - A formally documented mandatory legal or regulatory retention obligation may justify a narrowly scoped exception only with explicit authorization from the designated Legal Authority and independent Security review. - Any such exception must identify the legal basis, affected data, tenant, authorized scope, approving authority, and required retention period. - Legally retained content must remain excluded from AI retrieval unless separately and legitimately authorized. - Legal retention must not grant Platform Admin tenant-content access. - All exceptions and their subsequent release or expiry must be auditable.  5. RELATIONSHIP WITH Q4 RETENTION DEFERRALS  The retention details deferred during Q4 concerned lifecycle-specific retention periods for failed, rejected, superseded, expired, and overdue knowledge versions.  Those deferrals do not waive, suspend, or modify the separately established Q5 obligations:  - 24-hour primary-storage purge following explicit deletion approval. - Maximum 30-day encrypted-backup age-out from each backup's creation timestamp. - 365-day content-free audit retention from each audit record's creation timestamp.  The deferred lifecycle-specific retention schedule remains unresolved and requires separate governed clarification.  6. SECURITY AND GOVERNANCE CONSISTENCY  These requirements must preserve:  - Strict tenant isolation. - No exceptional Platform Admin tenant-content access in the first release. - Immediate retrieval exclusion after authorized deletion. - Prevention of deleted-content restoration. - Content-free and tamper-resistant audit evidence. - Controlled and independently authorized retention exceptions.  These decisions confirm the first-release backup and audit retention requirements. They do not authorize PRD approval, implementation, or any bypass of established deletion and access restrictions.,

rationale_deferrals.exact_rendered_segment: RATIONALE AND EXPLICIT REMAINING DEFERRALS — Q5 DELETION AND RETENTION  1. RATIONALE FOR THE FIRST-RELEASE POLICY  The selected deletion and retention policy provides a controlled, auditable, and tenant-isolated approach to managing knowledge content throughout its lifecycle.  It deliberately separates three different responsibilities:  - Immediate exclusion of deleted or ineligible content from AI retrieval and citation. - Physical removal of authorized deletion targets from active primary storage. - Limited retention of encrypted backups and content-free audit evidence.  This separation ensures that retaining historical or backup data does not imply continued permission to use that content for AI answers.  2. DELETION SCOPE AND AUTHORITY  Supporting both single-version deletion and entire logical document deletion provides operational flexibility while preventing accidental removal of unrelated versions.  Independent Tenant Admin authorization and controlled background execution establish accountability and reduce unauthorized or accidental deletion.  Platform Admins must not gain tenant-content access or deletion authority through administrative privileges.  3. RETRIEVAL SAFETY AND PHYSICAL PURGE  Immediate retrieval exclusion following explicit deletion approval ensures that deleted content cannot continue influencing AI-generated answers while physical deletion is in progress.  The mandatory 24-hour primary-storage purge requirement provides a measurable deletion deadline covering originals, extracted text, chunks, embeddings, indexes, caches, and other active derived copies.  Failure handling, retries, verification, and escalation ensure that deletion is not reported as successful before completion is established.  4. BACKUP AND AUDIT RETENTION RATIONALE  The maximum 30-day encrypted-backup age-out provides a bounded backup retention period without requiring deletion of unrelated content from shared backups.  The 365-day content-free audit retention provides evidence of deletion authorization, execution, failures, deadline breaches, verification, and accountability without preserving deleted business content.  Backup retention and audit retention are independent obligations with separate starting timestamps.  5. LIFECYCLE-STATE RETENTION RATIONALE  Failed, rejected, superseded, expired, and overdue content must remain excluded from AI retrieval.  Authorized human-only inspection may be permitted where operationally justified and explicitly authorized.  Physical retention and AI retrieval eligibility must remain separate decisions.  The mandatory 180-day independent re-review policy remains unchanged.  6. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED RETENTION DETAILS  The following lifecycle-specific retention durations remain unresolved:  - Failed document retention. - Rejected document retention. - Superseded version retention. - Expired document retention. - Overdue and pending-re-review content retention.  These periods require separate business, legal, regulatory, and operational assessment before being finalized.  Their deferral does not imply indefinite retention or override an authorized deletion request.  7. EXPLICITLY DEFERRED TECHNICAL DETAILS  The following implementation details are deferred to technical design:  - Exact backup infrastructure and automated expiry implementation. - Audit storage architecture and long-term evidence protection. - Component-specific deletion verification mechanisms. - Retry intervals, retry limits, and backoff configuration. - Monitoring, notification, and operational escalation SLAs. - Backup restoration validation implementation. - Detailed retention scheduling and lifecycle cleanup mechanisms.  These deferrals do not waive any established first-release deletion or retention obligation.  8. LEGAL HOLD AND RETENTION EXCEPTIONS  No legal hold, regulatory retention exception, or discretionary retention extension is implied merely because a requirement has been deferred.  The first release must not introduce an undocumented legal-hold or retention-exception bypass.  If a mandatory legal or regulatory retention obligation arises, it must be handled through a separately authorized and documented process that explicitly identifies:  - Applicable legal or regulatory basis. - Exact tenant and affected data scope. - Authorized approving Legal Authority. - Independent Security review. - Permitted retention duration and review conditions. - Access restrictions and AI retrieval exclusion. - Release or expiry conditions and audit evidence.  Any exception must remain limited to its explicitly approved scope and must not grant Platform Admin tenant-content access.  9. PRESERVATION OF PREVIOUS GOVERNANCE DECISIONS  All previously established Q2, Q3, and Q4 decisions remain unchanged, including:  - Independent non-submitter knowledge approval. - Mandatory 180-day re-review. - Tenant-scoped authorization and least privilege. - Prohibition of self-approval and privilege escalation. - Strict tenant isolation. - Prohibition of exceptional Platform Admin tenant-content access in the first release.  The Q4 technical and lifecycle retention deferrals do not waive the Q5 obligations.  The following Q5 requirements remain decided and mandatory:  - Immediate AI retrieval exclusion following authorized deletion. - Maximum 24-hour primary-storage purge. - Maximum 30-day encrypted-backup age-out. - 365-day content-free audit retention. - Verified deletion and controlled failure escalation.  10. FINAL FIRST-RELEASE POSITION  The first release prioritizes reliable deletion, immediate AI retrieval safety, bounded backup retention, content-free auditability, and strict tenant isolation.  Unresolved lifecycle-specific retention periods and technical implementation details remain explicitly deferred rather than assumed or silently waived.  These decisions clarify the Q5 requirements only. They do not constitute PRD approval, implementation authorization, or permission to bypass any established security or deletion control.
